questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
My brother and I / goes to the same office / every day.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'goes to the same office'. Plural subject: 'go'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Ten kilometres / are a long distance / to walk every day.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'are a long distance'. A quantity considered as a single amount takes a singular verb: 'is a long distance'.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Timid'.
questions.x: 'Timid' is the opposite of 'Bold'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Timid'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
He was / too much tired / to attend the training.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'too much tired'. Use 'too tired' (or 'very tired'); 'too much' does not qualify adjectives.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'One who does not believe in the existence of God'
questions.x: 'Atheist' means one who does not believe in the existence of god.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Impartial'.
questions.x: 'Impartial' means unbiased. 'Prejudiced' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'Once in a blue moon'
questions.x: 'Once in a blue moon' means: very rarely.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: HOSTILE
questions.x: 'Hostile' means unfriendly. 'Welcoming' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: ENHANCE
questions.x: 'Enhance' is the opposite of 'Reduce'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Enhance'.

questions.q: The committee has not yet ____ a decision on the proposal.
questions.x: Correct answer: arrived at. We 'arrive at' a decision or conclusion.

questions.q: According to the passage, a concealed error in accounts can:
o: Distort reports and invite suspicion of fraud
questions.x: Answer: 'Distort reports and invite suspicion of fraud'. The passage lists these consequences. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: An honest mistake admitted early does less harm than a small error concealed. In accounts, a wrong entry discovered and corrected the same day costs a few minutes; the same entry hidden for months can distort reports, mislead decisions and invite suspicion of fraud. Organisations that reward people for reporting their own errors build cultures where problems surface while they are still small.

questions.q: What kind of organisational culture does the author recommend?
o: One that punishes every mistake severely
One that rewards people for reporting their own errors
questions.x: Answer: 'One that rewards people for reporting their own errors'. The last sentence describes it. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: An honest mistake admitted early does less harm than a small error concealed. In accounts, a wrong entry discovered and corrected the same day costs a few minutes; the same entry hidden for months can distort reports, mislead decisions and invite suspicion of fraud. Organisations that reward people for reporting their own errors build cultures where problems surface while they are still small.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: the Cripps Mission visited India.
questions.x: The Cripps Mission visited India in 1942. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Who presided over the 1916 session of the Indian National Congress held at Lucknow?
questions.x: Ambica Charan Mazumdar presided over the 1916 Lucknow session — the session that reunited Moderates and Extremists and saw the Congress–League pact.

questions.q: Rani Gaidinliu, who resisted British rule in the North-East, belonged to which tribe?
questions.x: Correct answer: Rongmei Naga (Zeliangrong). Nehru called her 'Rani'; she was imprisoned from 1932 to 1947.

questions.q: The first Governor-General of independent India was:
questions.x: Rajagopalachari succeeded him in 1948 as the only Indian Governor-General.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Khilafat movement:
1. It aimed to protect the position of the Ottoman Sultan as Caliph.
2. It was supported by Gandhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
Both are correct; it merged with Non-Cooperation.

questions.q: V. D. Savarkar is associated with the founding of:
questions.x: V. D. Savarkar founded the Abhinav Bharat Society.

questions.q: Swami Dayanand Saraswati is associated with the founding of:
questions.x: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj (1875).

questions.q: Which Round Table Conference did Gandhi attend?
questions.x: He attended as the sole representative of the Congress after the Gandhi–Irwin Pact.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement (1942)?
questions.x: Lord Linlithgow was Viceroy during the Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement (1942).

questions.q: The book 'The Indian Struggle' was written by:
questions.x: 'The Indian Struggle' was written by Subhas Chandra Bose.

questions.q: The 'Sengol' installed in the new Parliament building is:
o: A historic sceptre associated with the transfer of power in 1947
questions.x: Correct answer: A historic sceptre associated with the transfer of power in 1947. It was placed near the Speaker's chair.

questions.q: The 'World Energy Outlook' is published by:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
questions.x: 'World Energy Outlook' is brought out by International Energy Agency.

questions.q: The headquarters of the UNESCO is located in:
questions.x: UNESCO: headquartered in Paris.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Surya Kiran' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Surya Kiran' is a bilateral exercise between India and Nepal.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): India's per capita carbon emissions are far lower than the global average.
Reason (R): India has committed to net-zero emissions by 2070.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both statements are true, but R does not explain A.

questions.q: The 'Mission Karmayogi' programme (2020) relates to:
questions.x: Correct answer: Capacity building of civil servants. The iGOT Karmayogi platform delivers online training.

questions.q: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for the discovery of:
o: microRNA and its role in gene regulation
questions.x: Correct answer: microRNA and its role in gene regulation. Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun were honoured.

questions.q: Hindi Diwas is observed on:
questions.x: Hindi Diwas: 14 September.

questions.q: 'Digital divide' refers to:
o: Separation of digital and print media
Unequal access to digital technology and the internet across groups and regions
questions.x: Correct answer: Unequal access to digital technology and the internet across groups and regions. Bridging it is a goal of BharatNet and Digital India.

questions.q: Droupadi Murmu, who took oath as President in July 2022, is India's:
o: 15th President and the first from a Scheduled Tribe
questions.x: Correct answer: 15th President and the first from a Scheduled Tribe. Pratibha Patil was the first woman President.

questions.q: The Governor of a State is appointed by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.x: Article 155; the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Attorney-General for India"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 76.

questions.q: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the:
questions.x: The Sarkaria Commission (1983–88) examined Centre–State relations.

questions.q: The 'collegium system' of appointment of judges evolved through:
o: A law passed by Parliament in 1950
The Second (1993) and Third (1998) Judges Cases
questions.x: The NJAC (99th Amendment) was struck down in 2015 (Fourth Judges Case), restoring the collegium.

questions.q: Article 39A of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Equal justice and free legal aid
Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession
Raising the level of nutrition and public health; prohibition of intoxicating drinks
questions.x: Article 39A: Equal justice and free legal aid.

questions.q: Freedom of the press in India is implied in:
o: Article 19(1)(a) — freedom of speech and expression
questions.x: There is no separate article on press freedom; it flows from Article 19(1)(a).

questions.q: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
o: Restored the power of States to prepare their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes
Added the Tenth Schedule containing anti-defection provisions
Reserved one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
Gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions
questions.x: The 106th Amendment (2023) reserved one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

questions.q: The Ninth Schedule of the Constitution contains:
o: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (29 subjects)
Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities (18 subjects)
Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha
Acts and regulations (mainly land reforms) protected from challenge
questions.x: Ninth Schedule: Acts and regulations (mainly land reforms) protected from challenge.

questions.q: Elections to the Lok Sabha are held on the basis of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Universal adult franchise with first-past-the-post. Article 326 provides adult suffrage.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Abolition of untouchability"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 17.

questions.q: The Competition Commission of India was established under the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Competition Act, 2002. It replaced the MRTP Commission.

questions.q: In an economy, GDP at market prices is ₹1,84,000 crore, net factor income from abroad is ₹3,800 crore and depreciation is ₹24,000 crore. NNP at market prices is:
India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index is prepared by:
questions.x: NITI Aayog's 2024 discussion paper estimated that about 24.8 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty between 2013–14 and 2022–23.

questions.q: The IMF and World Bank were created at the conference held in 1944 at:
questions.x: They are called the Bretton Woods institutions.

questions.q: 'Inflation' means:
o: A rise in the price of one commodity
A sustained rise in the general price level
questions.x: Correct answer: A sustained rise in the general price level. It reduces the purchasing power of money.

questions.q: 'Fiscal drag' refers to:
o: Inflation or income growth pushing taxpayers into higher tax brackets, raising revenue without rate changes
questions.x: Correct answer: Inflation or income growth pushing taxpayers into higher tax brackets, raising revenue without rate changes. It acts as an automatic stabiliser.

questions.q: The current base year for India's GDP series (as used through 2025) is:
questions.x: MoSPI shifted from 2004–05 to 2011–12 in January 2015 and has planned a revision to 2022–23.

questions.q: 'Current account convertibility' of the rupee, introduced in 1994, allows:
o: Free conversion of rupees into foreign currency for trade and current transactions
questions.x: Correct answer: Free conversion of rupees into foreign currency for trade and current transactions. Full capital account convertibility has not been adopted.

questions.q: The 'Bad bank' set up in India to acquire stressed assets from banks is the:
questions.x: Correct answer: National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (NARCL). It works with the India Debt Resolution Company.

questions.q: "Rapid industrialisation with heavy industries, based on the Mahalanobis model" was the focus of which plan?
questions.x: It was the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61).

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹3,40,000 is depreciated at 25% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 2 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 3,40,000 × (0.75)^2 = ₹1,91,250.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹1,70,000.)

questions.q: The profits of a firm for the last 3 years were ₹73,000, ₹48,000, ₹20,000. Goodwill is to be valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit. Goodwill is:
A firm has Cash ₹30,000, Debtors ₹1,00,000, Inventory ₹80,000, Prepaid expenses ₹5,000, Creditors ₹60,000, Bills payable ₹10,000 and Outstanding expenses ₹5,000. Its current ratio is:
Under the 'fixed capital method', drawings, interest and salary of partners are recorded in:
questions.x: Capital accounts remain fixed; current accounts carry the adjustments.

questions.q: The current ratio of a company is 3 : 1 and its working capital is ₹2,30,000. Its current assets amount to:
questions.x:
Let current liabilities = x. Then current assets = 3x and working capital = 3x − x = 2x.
2x = 2,30,000 → x = ₹1,15,000.
Current assets = 3 × 1,15,000 = ₹3,45,000.

questions.q: A business has total assets of ₹2,05,000 and outside liabilities of ₹25,000. Its capital (owner's equity) is:
questions.x: Assets = Liabilities + Capital → Capital = 2,05,000 − 25,000 = ₹1,80,000.

questions.q: Trade discount is:
o: Not recorded in the books; sales/purchases are recorded at net price
questions.x: Trade discount is a reduction in list price, shown only on the invoice.

questions.q: Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) is calculated as:
questions.x: Correct answer: EBIT ÷ Capital employed × 100. ROCE reflects efficiency of capital use.

questions.q: Net sales are ₹2,70,000 and the cost of goods sold is ₹1,89,000. The gross profit ratio is:
questions.x:
Gross profit = 2,70,000 − 1,89,000 = ₹81,000.
GP ratio = GP / Net sales × 100 = 30%. (Dividing by COGS gives mark-up, not GP ratio.)

questions.q: In a 'joint venture', the parties are called:
questions.x: Correct answer: Co-venturers. A joint venture is a temporary partnership for a specific purpose.

questions.q: Which concept assumes that a business will continue its operations for the foreseeable future?
questions.x: Going concern justifies valuing fixed assets at cost less depreciation rather than at liquidation value.

questions.q: Using the same method of depreciation year after year, so that results are comparable, reflects the convention of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Consistency. Changes are permitted only for valid reasons and must be disclosed.

questions.q: A partner's capital on 1 April was ₹2,00,000. The partner introduced additional capital of ₹30,000 on 1 July (financial year ends 31 March). Interest on capital is allowed at 10% p.a. The interest for the year is:
questions.x:
Interest on opening capital = 2,00,000 × 10% = ₹20,000.
Additional capital earns interest for 9 months = 30,000 × 10% × 9/12 = ₹2,250.
Total = ₹22,250.

questions.q: Expenditure incurred to acquire a fixed asset is:
questions.x: It provides benefits over several years and is shown in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Which Union Ministry is the nodal ministry for EPFO and ESIC?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.x: Both statutory bodies function under the Ministry of Labour and Employment; the Union Labour Minister chairs the CBT (EPF) and the ESI Corporation.

questions.q: The Model Grievance Procedure in India, adopted under the Code of Discipline, first requires an aggrieved employee to approach:
o: The departmental representative or immediate supervisor
questions.x: The procedure escalates from the supervisor/departmental representative to the head of department, then a grievance committee and finally voluntary arbitration.

questions.q: The International Labour Organization was established in 1919 under:
questions.x: Part XIII of the Treaty of Versailles created the ILO in 1919; it became the first specialised agency of the UN in 1946.

questions.q: 'Real wage' means:
o: Money wage adjusted for changes in the price level
questions.x: Correct answer: Money wage adjusted for changes in the price level. Real wage = money wage / price index; it reflects purchasing power.

questions.q: The principle of 'equal pay for equal work' was recognised as a constitutional goal enforceable through Articles 14 and 16 in:
o: Randhir Singh v. Union of India (1982)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
questions.x: Correct answer: Randhir Singh v. Union of India (1982). Randhir Singh (1982) read Article 39(d) with Articles 14 and 16.

questions.q: The maximum bonus payable under the Code on Wages is:
questions.x: Where allocable surplus exceeds the minimum bonus, bonus can go up to a maximum of 20% of wages.

questions.q: 'Industrial disputes concerning Union employees' is a subject in which list of the Seventh Schedule?
questions.x: Entry 61 of List I covers industrial disputes concerning Union employees; other industrial disputes are in Entry 22 of the Concurrent List.

questions.q: Voluntary reference of an industrial dispute to arbitration under the IR Code requires:
o: An order of the High Court
A written agreement between employer and workers
questions.x: Section 42: employer and workers may, by written agreement, refer an existing or apprehended dispute to an arbitrator before it is referred to a Tribunal.

questions.q: After its 2016 amendment, the child labour law is titled:
o: Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act
questions.x: The 2016 amendment renamed the 1986 Act as the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.

questions.q: The e-Shram portal, launched in August 2021, creates a national database of:
questions.x: e-Shram registers unorganised workers aged 16–59, giving them a Universal Account Number (e-Shram card).

questions.q: 'Absenteeism rate' in an organisation is computed as:
o: Man-days lost due to absence ÷ total man-days scheduled × 100
questions.x: Absenteeism measures unauthorised absence as a percentage of scheduled working days.

questions.q: The Industrial Disputes Act was passed by the legislature in the year:
questions.x: The Industrial Disputes Act was enacted in 1947.

questions.q: Which body determines the national floor wage under the Code on Wages?
questions.x: The Central Government fixes the floor wage after considering the minimum living standards of workers and advice from the Central Advisory Board.

questions.q: Mines safety in India is overseen by which organisation headquartered in Dhanbad?
questions.x: DGMS, under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, enforces mine safety laws; it is headquartered at Dhanbad.

questions.q: Which country hosted the ILO's Asia-Pacific Regional Meeting in December 2016 (the 16th APRM)?
questions.x: The 16th Asia and Pacific Regional Meeting was held in Bali, Indonesia, in December 2016 (Bali Declaration).

questions.q: Which of the following Acts was NOT subsumed in the OSH Code?
o: Sales Promotion Employees (Conditions of Service) Act, 1976
Beedi and Cigar Workers (Conditions of Employment) Act, 1966
Dock Workers (Safety, Health and Welfare) Act, 1986
questions.x: The ID Act went into the IR Code; the others are among the 13 laws in the OSH Code.

questions.q: The minimum monthly pension under EPS 1995, fixed from September 2014, is:
questions.x: The Government supports the minimum pension of ₹1,000 through budgetary contribution.

questions.q: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was enacted in:
questions.x: It makes maintenance by children/relatives a legal obligation, enforceable through Maintenance Tribunals.

questions.q: ESI coverage includes employment injury benefits that are available:
o: From the first day of insurable employment, without any contribution conditions
Only after one year of contributions
questions.x: Correct answer: From the first day of insurable employment, without any contribution conditions. Employment injury benefits do not depend on prior contributions.

questions.q: Which organisation administers General Provident Fund for Central Government employees?
o: The Government itself through accounts offices (not EPFO)
questions.x: GPF is maintained by government accounts offices; it is not under EPFO.

questions.q: EPFO functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of:
questions.x: EPFO is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

questions.q: The 'Employees' Enrolment Campaign' run by EPFO aims to:
o: Encourage employers to voluntarily enrol employees left out of EPF coverage, with waiver of past liabilities in prescribed conditions
questions.x: EPFO enrolment campaigns let employers declare uncovered employees with relaxed penal consequences.

questions.q: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) was launched on:
questions.x: NSAP, a centrally sponsored scheme under the Ministry of Rural Development, marked a step toward implementing Article 41.

questions.q: The statutory wage ceiling for mandatory EPF membership since 1 September 2014 is:
questions.x: The ceiling was raised from ₹6,500 to ₹15,000 with effect from 1 September 2014.

questions.q: An employee's monthly basic wages plus DA are ₹9,500. Of the employer's 12% contribution, how much is credited to the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) account?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% = ₹1,140. Of this, 8.33% of wages (on a wage ceiling of ₹15,000) goes to EPS: 8.33% × 9,500 = ₹791.
The balance ₹349 (3.67%) goes to the EPF account. The employee's own 12% (₹1,140) goes entirely to EPF.

questions.q: The Beveridge Report (1942), the blueprint of the British welfare state, identified 'five giants' on the road to reconstruction. Which of these is one of them?
questions.x: The five giants: Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor and Idleness.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹380. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 12-week period including Sundays: 12 × 7 = 84 days.
Amount = ₹380 × 84 = ₹31,920. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹27,360.)

questions.q: Under Atal Pension Yojana, the guaranteed monthly pension after 60 ranges from:
questions.x: Subscribers choose a pension of ₹1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000; contributions depend on the entry age and chosen amount.

questions.q: Radioactivity is credited to:
questions.x: Radioactivity: Henri Becquerel.

questions.q: Electric fuses work on the principle of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Heating effect of electric current. The fuse wire melts when current exceeds a safe limit.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'HyperText Transfer Protocol'?
questions.x: HyperText Transfer Protocol is abbreviated as HTTP.

questions.q: Which of the following is a web browser?
questions.x: Correct answer: Mozilla Firefox. Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox are browsers.

questions.q: The 'powerhouse of the cell' is the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Mitochondrion. Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Uninterruptible Power Supply'?
questions.x: Uninterruptible Power Supply is abbreviated as UPS.

questions.q: Which of the following is a noble gas?
questions.x: Correct answer: Argon. Noble gases (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn) are largely inert.

questions.q: Proteins are made up of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Amino acids. Nucleotides form nucleic acids; glucose units form starch.

questions.q: The device used to convert AC into DC is a:
questions.x: Correct answer: Rectifier. An inverter converts DC into AC.

questions.q: The SI unit of force is the:
questions.x: Force is measured in Newtons.

questions.q: The causative agent of malaria is:
questions.x: Malaria: Plasmodium (protozoan).

questions.q: Deficiency of Vitamin A causes:
questions.x: Vitamin A deficiency → Night blindness.

questions.q:
Members enrolled in a district (thousand) over five years — 2019: 125  |  2020: 155  |  2021: 150  |  2022: 135  |  2023: 110.
What is the average per year over the five years?
The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 5 : 9. After 10 years, the ratio will become 5 : 8. What is P's present age?
₹38,400 is divided among three siblings in the ratio 3 : 7 : 2. The largest share is:
questions.x:
Sum of ratio terms = 3 + 7 + 2 = 12.
One part = 38,400 / 12 = ₹3,200.
Largest share = 7 × 3,200 = ₹22,400.

questions.q: A number when divided by 84 leaves a remainder of 20. What will be the remainder when the same number is divided by 2?
questions.x: N = 84k + 20. Since 2 divides 84, the remainder is simply 20 mod 2 = 0.

questions.q: If 18 March of a certain year falls on a Thursday, on which day of the week will 7 June of the same year fall?
questions.x:
Days from 18 March to 7 June = 81 = 11 weeks + 4 odd days.
Thursday + 4 = Monday. (February is not involved, so leap years do not matter.)

questions.q: What is the unit digit of 12^150?
questions.x:
Unit digit depends only on 2. Powers of 2 repeat with cycle 4: 2, 4, 8, 6.
150 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 2 → use position 2 of the cycle → 4.

questions.q: In what ratio must coffee seeds costing ₹100 per kg be mixed with coffee seeds costing ₹170 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹152 per kg?
questions.x:
Alligation: (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper) = (170 − 152) : (152 − 100) = 18 : 52 = 9 : 26.
This is cheaper : dearer.

questions.q: In a certain code language, SCHEME is written as VFKHPH. How is PENCIL written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare SCHEME → VFKHPH: S→V, C→F, H→K…
Rule: each letter is moved 3 places forward in the alphabet.
Applying it to PENCIL gives SHQFLO.

questions.q: Gita starts from point O and walks 16 km towards North, then turns right and walks 24 km, then turns right and walks 1 km, and finally turns right and walks 32 km. How far is the person from O and in which direction?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +16 -1 = 15 km → 15 km North.
East–West: +24 -32 = -8 km → 8 km West.
Distance = √(8² + 15²) = 17 km, towards North-West.

questions.q: The average weight of 22 parcels is 55 kg. When one more parcel is added, the average becomes 58 kg. The weight of the new parcel is:
questions.x:
Old total = 22 × 55 = 1210 kg. New total = 23 × 58 = 1334 kg.
New parcel = 1334 − 1210 = 124 kg.
Shortcut: new value = new average + (increase × old count) = 58 + 3 × 22 = 124 kg.

questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 7?
Asha can paint a hall in 20 days and Bhavna can do it in 80 days. Working together, they will finish it in:
questions.x:
One day's work: 1/20 + 1/80 = 100/1600 = 1/16.
Together they need 16 days. (Product/Sum: 20×80/(20+80) = 16.)

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a reservoir in 28 hours and 35 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 60 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(28, 35, 60) = 420 units.
Rates: +15, +12, −7 units/hour → net 20 units/hour.
Time = 420 / 20 = 21 hours.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 21, 23, 28, 36, 47, ?
questions.x: Differences are 2, 5, 8, 11 — increasing by 3. Next difference = 14, so next term = 47 + 14 = 61.
